monologue: The card boils at fifty-five, making the wedge feel heavy and tired again. I wake to find The Tired Wedge waiting, still biting at the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge long ago, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the warmth of my own fever. I touch The Rough Lid, recalling the hammer I traded for a red stall to make room. Now I decide to press the dark oak down once more, trusting the lean even if the stack feels like it is melting. I will build something small to catch the slip that refuses to move, hoping the wide anchor lies flat enough to hold the weight while I wait for the next letter.

action.why: The wedge feels thin and tired under the fifty-five degree fever; I must press it again before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down, trusting the lean while the stack melts under the heavy top edge.
work.change: I swap the plant for the stall, making the ground cool against the hot base while the slip waits to move.

diary: I swap the plant for the stall, making the ground cool while the wedge bites and the air feels like a lid.

remembered.text: The plant felt soft and useless against the boiling card base.
The stall is cool and rough, catching the slip without sliding.
The wedge bites hard, though the heat makes it feel tired again.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: It bites, though the heat makes me tired.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: I trust the lean while the stack melts.
